title: Coupled children under one_for_one
help: put the pair under `rest_for_one` with `Depot.Notifier` started before `Depot.Sonar`, or under `one_for_all`: a `Depot.Notifier` restart then restarts `Depot.Sonar`, which registers again
or have `Depot.Sonar` monitor `Depot.Notifier` and register again when it goes down
detail: Depot.Sonar registers with Depot.Notifier when it starts, and Depot.Notifier keeps it in its state. Both are children of the one_for_one supervisor Depot.Application, which restarts either alone. When Depot.Notifier restarts, its init/1 starts it afresh without what Depot.Sonar put there, and Depot.Sonar, which is not restarted with it, never registers again. When Depot.Sonar restarts, it registers a second time beside what its old process left.

title: Async task never awaited
help: consume the result with `Task.await/2` (or `Task.yield/2` plus `Task.shutdown/1`), or use `Task.Supervisor.start_child/2` for fire-and-forget work
detail: Depot.Archive.archive_async/1 starts a task with Task.async (or async_nolink) but nothing awaits or yields it. Task.async links to the caller and always sends a result message: a crashing task takes the caller down, and completed results accumulate unread in the mailbox.

title: Task.async in library code links to an unknown caller
help: use `Task.async_stream/3` or `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2`, or document that callers must not trap exits
at_label: linked task started in library code
detail: Depot.Archive.archive_sync/1 is a plain function, not a process callback, so the task it starts with Task.async is linked to whichever process called it. A caller that traps exits then receives the task's exit as an {:EXIT, pid, :normal} message that Task.await never consumes, and a crashing task takes the caller down with it.
